books.title: Understanding Society: India and Beyond — Social Science Textbook for Grade 9, Part 1
books.edition: First Edition, June 2026 (Jyeshtha 1948) — new NCERT book for the 2026-27 session

source.method: chapter titles from the book's Contents page; topics from each chapter PDF's section headings

chapters.title: Understanding Social Science
chapters.book: Understanding Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: What is Social Science? Social Science in Everyday Life
objectives: Student can describe Social Science as the systematic study of human society and how it differs from the natural sciences
Student can trace how everyday activities, such as eating, travelling and studying, depend on systems of governance, economy, society and environment
visualIdeas: a day in a student’s life with arrows to the farmer, road authority, school policy and power station behind each activity

topics.title: Understanding Society through Time and Traditions
objectives: Student can describe how societies changed from early communities to villages, towns and cities
Student can explain how Indian knowledge traditions, such as the idea of the Pañchamahābhūtas and the Arthaśhāstra, reflect early systematic thinking about nature, governance and the economy
visualIdeas: a timeline from early hunter-gatherers to modern cities

topics.title: Social Science as a Study of Disciplines: Geography and History
objectives: Student can explain why a problem like drought needs several disciplines to understand it
Student can describe what Geography studies
Student can classify sources of history as literary, archaeological, epigraphic and numismatic with an example of each
visualIdeas: four cards: a palm-leaf manuscript, a terracotta figurine, a Brahmi inscription and a Samudragupta coin

topics.title: Social Science as a Study of Disciplines: Political Science and Economics
objectives: Student can describe what Political Science studies, with Panchayati Raj as an example of grassroots democracy
Student can describe what Economics studies and outline India’s economic journey before and after colonial rule
visualIdeas: a village panchayat meeting beside a market scene

topics.title: Why Should We Study Social Science? Its Future
objectives: Student can explain how Social Science helps citizens take part in civic life and ask informed questions about shared challenges
Student can describe the role of Social Science in addressing issues such as climate change and new technologies
visualIdeas: a bridge linking past, present and future

chapters.title: Shaping of the Earth's Surface
chapters.book: Understanding Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: Plate Tectonics: The Earth’s Layers and Plates
objectives: Student can name the layers of the Earth: crust, mantle and core
Student can explain that the crust is broken into plates that move
visualIdeas: a cut-away Earth showing crust, mantle and core
a world map of the major plates

topics.title: Plate Tectonics: Earthquakes, Volcanoes, Folding and Faulting
objectives: Student can explain how interior forces such as earthquakes, volcanoes, folding and faulting move and shape the crust
Student can relate the Himalaya to the folding of rock layers
visualIdeas: rock layers folding into mountains and breaking along a fault

topics.title: Weathering and Erosion
objectives: Student can distinguish weathering (breaking down without movement) from erosion (wearing away and carrying material)
Student can describe physical, chemical and biological weathering and the types of erosion
Student can explain how erosion affects farmers, people near rivers and coasts, and other occupations
visualIdeas: a rock cracking from frost beside a river carrying sediment away

topics.title: Agents of Gradation: Running Water
objectives: Student can name the agents of gradation
Student can describe landforms made by rivers, such as waterfalls, V-shaped valleys, meanders, ox-bow lakes, floodplains and deltas
visualIdeas: a river’s course from mountain to sea with a waterfall, meander, ox-bow lake and delta

topics.title: Agents of Gradation: Waves and Currents
objectives: Student can describe coastal landforms made by waves and currents, such as beaches, sand bars, cliffs, sea caves, arches and stacks
Student can explain how beaches matter to people, from tourism and fishing to protection against coastal erosion
visualIdeas: a headland eroding into a sea cave, then an arch, then a stack

topics.title: Agents of Gradation: Glaciers
objectives: Student can describe landforms of glacial erosion such as U-shaped valleys, cirques, aretes, hanging valleys and fjords, and deposits such as moraines
Student can explain how glacial landforms are useful to people, for example for tourism and harbours
visualIdeas: a glacier flowing down a U-shaped valley with a moraine at its snout

topics.title: Agents of Gradation: Wind
objectives: Student can explain how strong winds pick up and carry loose sand and soil in dry areas
Student can describe landforms made by wind, such as yardangs, ventifacts and sand dunes
visualIdeas: a desert scene with sand dunes and a wind-carved rock

topics.title: Agents of Gradation: Underground Water
objectives: Student can explain how underground water dissolves limestone to form karst topography
Student can describe karst landforms such as caves, stalactites, stalagmites and sinkholes
visualIdeas: a limestone cave with stalactites hanging and stalagmites rising

topics.title: Landforms and Disasters: Landslides and Avalanches
objectives: Student can explain the natural and human causes of landslides
Student can explain the causes of avalanches on snow-covered slopes
visualIdeas: a hillside with heavy rain and a road cut, showing a slope failing

topics.title: Landforms and Disasters: GLOFs and Dust Storms
objectives: Student can explain what a glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) is and why it happens
Student can explain the causes of dust storms in desert and semi-arid regions and suggest mitigation measures
visualIdeas: a glacial lake held by a moraine wall that breaks and floods the valley

chapters.title: Atmosphere and Climate
chapters.book: Understanding Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: Composition of the Atmosphere
objectives: Student can name the main gases of the atmosphere and the role of water vapour and dust
Student can explain how the atmosphere supports life and helps form clouds and rain
visualIdeas: a pie chart of atmospheric gases: nitrogen, oxygen and others

topics.title: Structure of the Atmosphere
objectives: Student can name the layers of the atmosphere: troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere
Student can explain that the layers are divided by changes in temperature and air density with height
visualIdeas: a layered column of the atmosphere with heights and a temperature line

topics.title: Weather and Climate
objectives: Student can distinguish weather from climate
Student can describe the elements of weather and climate, such as temperature, pressure, wind, humidity and rainfall
visualIdeas: a daily weather card beside a 30-year climate graph

topics.title: Seasons in India
objectives: Student can describe India’s tropical monsoon climate
Student can name the four seasons used by the India Meteorological Department: winter, summer, monsoon and post-monsoon
Student can describe the six traditional Indian seasons based on the Indian calendar
visualIdeas: a circular calendar of India’s four seasons

topics.title: Monsoon
objectives: Student can explain the monsoon as a seasonal reversal of winds and why it matters to India
Student can describe traditional methods of predicting rainfall in texts such as the Kṛiṣhiparāśhara and the Bṛihatsaṁhitā
visualIdeas: a map of India with the monsoon winds arriving from the south-west

topics.title: Climate Change
objectives: Student can explain climate change as a long-term change caused mainly by human activities such as burning fuels and cutting trees
Student can suggest ways to reduce one’s carbon footprint
visualIdeas: a footprint made of icons: car, electricity, plastic, food

topics.title: Punjab Floods 2025: A Case Study
objectives: Student can describe the causes and effects of the 2025 floods in Punjab
Student can discuss how extreme weather affects people and how communities can prepare
visualIdeas: a map of Punjab with flooded districts marked

chapters.title: Early Humans and Beginning of Civilisation
chapters.book: Understanding Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: Why Should We Study Early Human History?
objectives: Student can explain that early human history covers the long period before the invention of writing
Student can describe how archaeologists study this period through tools, fossils and cave art
visualIdeas: a timeline split at the invention of writing

topics.title: Who Were Our Human Ancestors?
objectives: Student can explain that early humans evolved in Africa and gradually migrated to other parts of the world
Student can name early human species such as Homo erectus and Homo sapiens
visualIdeas: a world map with migration arrows out of Africa

topics.title: Palaeolithic Hunter-Gatherers
objectives: Student can describe the life of Palaeolithic hunter-gatherers
Student can name their stone tools, such as handaxes, cleavers and scrapers, and where they lived
visualIdeas: a handaxe and a cleaver with labels
a cave shelter with a fire

topics.title: Mesolithic Hunter-Gatherers
objectives: Student can describe the microlithic tools of the Mesolithic period
Student can describe their temporary settlements near rivers and lakes and their rock art at sites like Bhimbetka
visualIdeas: microliths hafted onto a wooden shaft

topics.title: The Neolithic Revolution and the Neolithic in the Indian Subcontinent
objectives: Student can explain why the shift to farming and domestication of animals is called the Neolithic Revolution
Student can describe Neolithic sites in the subcontinent such as Mehrgarh and Burzahom
Student can describe the Chalcolithic use of copper with stone tools
visualIdeas: a Neolithic village with fields, animals, pottery and weaving

topics.title: Sindhu-Sarasvatī Civilisation
objectives: Student can describe the planned cities, drainage, seals and crafts of the Sindhu-Sarasvatī Civilisation
Student can name major sites such as Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira, Lothal and Rakhigarhi
visualIdeas: a city grid with drains and a seal

topics.title: Bronze Age Civilisations: Mesopotamia
objectives: Student can describe the features of Bronze Age civilisations: cities, trade, writing and administration
Student can describe Mesopotamian achievements such as cuneiform writing, ziggurats and Hammurabi’s laws
visualIdeas: a clay tablet with cuneiform signs beside a ziggurat

topics.title: Egyptian Civilisation
objectives: Student can explain the importance of the Nile to Egyptian civilisation
Student can describe pharaohs, pyramids, mummification and papyrus records
visualIdeas: the Nile valley with pyramids and a papyrus scroll

topics.title: The Chinese Civilisation
objectives: Student can describe the growth of Chinese civilisation along the Huang He (Yellow River)
Student can describe the Shang period, bronze work and the logographic Chinese script
visualIdeas: a map of the Huang He valley with a bronze vessel

chapters.title: State and Society up to 1000 CE
chapters.book: Understanding Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: Understanding Early Indian State and Society
objectives: Student can describe the continuity of cultural, social and political traditions in Indian civilisation
Student can identify the sources historians use to study early Indian states
visualIdeas: a timeline of Indian states up to 1000 CE

topics.title: The Vedic Period and its Political Institutions
objectives: Student can describe clans (janas) led by a rājā in the Vedic period
Student can describe the role of assemblies such as the sabhā and samiti
visualIdeas: a Vedic assembly with elders in discussion

topics.title: Early Kingdoms and Republics
objectives: Student can explain how janapadas grew into larger kingdoms such as Magadha
Student can describe republics (gaṇas or saṅghas) and how they differed from kingdoms
visualIdeas: a map of the janapadas and mahājanapadas with Magadha highlighted

topics.title: Duties and Ideals of the King
objectives: Student can describe the duties expected of a king, such as protecting subjects and administering justice
Student can use sources such as the Arthaśhāstra and the Śhānti Parva of the Mahābhārata to explain ideals of kingship
visualIdeas: a king seated with symbols of justice and welfare

topics.title: Council of Ministers
objectives: Student can describe the role of the council of ministers in governance
Student can name the seven constituents (saptāṅga) of the state in the Arthaśhāstra and explain the saying that one wheel does not move the carriage
visualIdeas: a king with ministers each holding a different responsibility

topics.title: How Were Empires Administered?
objectives: Student can describe the administration, taxation and military organisation of empires such as the Mauryas, Guptas and Cholas
Student can describe local self-government through village assemblies, such as in the Uttaramerur inscription
visualIdeas: an organisation chart from emperor to provinces to villages

topics.title: Ethics: The Foundation of Law and Life
objectives: Student can explain dharma as duty, righteousness and moral conduct rather than religion
Student can describe how Aśhoka’s dhamma and later records linked ethics with governance
visualIdeas: an Aśhokan pillar with an edict

topics.title: Social Structures: Varṇa and Jāti
objectives: Student can describe the varṇa system and the factors, such as occupation, region and gotra, that shaped social identity
Student can read a source like a Ṛigveda verse for evidence, interpretation and its limits
visualIdeas: a web of factors shaping social identity: occupation, region, language, gotra

topics.title: Family, Society and the Role of Women
objectives: Student can describe family and social life in early India
Student can describe the roles and status of women in early Indian society
visualIdeas: a household scene showing different family roles

topics.title: Religious Life, Bhakti and the Quest for Knowledge
objectives: Student can describe the emergence of the Bhakti tradition
Student can describe education in early India, from gurukulas to centres of learning, and the subjects studied
visualIdeas: a gurukula scene with students and a teacher

topics.title: Literary Heritage of Early India
objectives: Student can name important early Indian texts on grammar, law and ethics, and medicine, such as Pāṇini’s Aṣhṭādhyāyī and the Charaka Saṁhitā
Student can name works of Sanskrit poetry and Tamil literature, such as the works of Kālidāsa, the Tirukkural and the Sangam texts
visualIdeas: a shelf of manuscripts labelled Aṣhṭādhyāyī, Charaka Saṁhitā and others

topics.title: Economy: Agriculture, Land Revenue and Irrigation
objectives: Student can explain that the early economy was based on agriculture supported by land revenue
Student can describe irrigation works such as the Sudarshana lake and the Grand Anicut (Kallanai)
visualIdeas: a canal and dam watering fields

topics.title: Trade Routes, Ports and Guilds
objectives: Student can describe trade routes and ports such as Muziris and their role in commerce
Student can describe guilds and how they also worked as financial institutions
visualIdeas: a map of trade routes and ports around the Indian Ocean

chapters.title: Democracy
chapters.book: Understanding Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: Tracing Democratic Traditions from Early Times
objectives: Student can describe democracy as a system of self-governance that is more than elections
Student can describe early democratic traditions in India, such as the sabhā and samiti, and how ideas from the world shaped modern democracy
visualIdeas: a timeline from Vedic assemblies to the Indian Constitution

topics.title: Principles of Democracy: Popular Sovereignty, Rule of Law and Fundamental Rights
objectives: Student can explain popular sovereignty and universal adult franchise
Student can explain the rule of law and the role of fundamental rights
visualIdeas: three pillars labelled popular sovereignty, rule of law and fundamental rights

topics.title: Principles of Democracy: Separation of Powers, Accountability and Multi-Party System
objectives: Student can explain the separation of powers between legislature, executive and judiciary
Student can explain accountability and transparency, including the Right to Information
Student can explain the multi-party system and the safeguarding of the rights of vulnerable groups
visualIdeas: three branches of government with checks between them

topics.title: Types of Democracy
objectives: Student can distinguish direct democracy from representative democracy
Student can compare parliamentary and presidential democracies with examples
visualIdeas: a two-column comparison: parliamentary (India, Canada) and presidential (USA)

topics.title: Democracy in Practice: India’s Living Democracy
objectives: Student can explain why India is called the world’s largest democracy
Student can describe democracy at the local level through panchayats and the representation of women
visualIdeas: a graphic of India’s voter count beside a panchayat meeting

topics.title: Challenges to Democratic Practices in India; Democracy and You
objectives: Student can describe challenges to democratic practices such as misinformation on social media
Student can describe how citizens contribute to democracy through civic awareness and responsible use of media
visualIdeas: a phone screen with a fake news alert and a fact-check

chapters.title: Elections
chapters.book: Understanding Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: Why do Elections Matter?
objectives: Student can explain why elections are called the soul of democracy
Student can explain that voting is both a constitutional right and a duty
visualIdeas: a ballot box with diverse hands dropping votes

topics.title: The Electoral System
objectives: Student can explain the first-past-the-post system used in India
Student can compare it with proportional representation
visualIdeas: a constituency result showing the candidate with the most votes winning

topics.title: The Laws and the Delimitation Commission
objectives: Student can describe the role of the Representation of the People Acts of 1950 and 1951
Student can explain how the Delimitation Commission draws constituencies
visualIdeas: a map divided into constituencies

topics.title: Election Commission of India (ECI)
objectives: Student can describe the role of the ECI in conducting free and fair elections
Student can describe the electoral roll, voter ID, the Model Code of Conduct and EVMs with VVPAT
visualIdeas: an EVM with a VVPAT slip

topics.title: Political Parties
objectives: Student can explain the role of political parties in presenting programmes and policies through manifestos
Student can distinguish national and state parties and describe party symbols
visualIdeas: a set of election symbols beside a manifesto

topics.title: Challenges to Free and Fair Elections
objectives: Student can identify challenges to free and fair elections
Student can describe how the ECI tries to ensure that elections are impartial
visualIdeas: a checklist of challenges with the ECI’s responses

chapters.title: Building Blocks in Economics: The Problem of Choice
chapters.book: Understanding Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: Choices and Limited Resources
objectives: Student can explain that resources are limited while wants are unlimited, so we must make choices
Student can define opportunity cost with everyday examples
visualIdeas: a student choosing between two items with one budget, the forgone item labelled opportunity cost

topics.title: What does Economics Deal with?
objectives: Student can explain the origin of the word economics from the Greek oikonomia (household management)
Student can describe how consumers, producers, governments and financial institutions make choices with limited resources, and what economists do
visualIdeas: a household, a firm and a government each making a choice

topics.title: Key Questions in Economics
objectives: Student can state the central questions of what to produce, how to produce and for whom to produce
Student can distinguish labour-intensive from capital-intensive ways of production
visualIdeas: three question cards: what, how and for whom

topics.title: Economic Systems: Planned, Market and Mixed Economy
objectives: Student can describe how planned, market and mixed economies answer the central questions
Student can explain why India is described as a mixed economy
visualIdeas: three boxes: government decides, market decides, both decide

chapters.title: The Price Puzzle: What Drives the Market
chapters.book: Understanding Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: Demand and the Law of Demand
objectives: Student can define demand and read a demand schedule and demand curve
Student can state the law of demand: as price falls, quantity demanded rises
visualIdeas: a downward-sloping demand curve with a schedule beside it

topics.title: Other Determinants of Demand
objectives: Student can explain how income, tastes, seasons, future expectations and population affect demand
Student can distinguish substitute goods from complementary goods and explain how their prices affect demand
visualIdeas: tea and coffee as substitutes, smartphones and earphones as complements

topics.title: Supply and the Law of Supply
objectives: Student can define supply and read a supply schedule and supply curve
Student can state the law of supply: as price rises, quantity supplied rises
visualIdeas: an upward-sloping supply curve with a schedule beside it

topics.title: Other Determinants of Supply
objectives: Student can explain how prices of related goods and the number of sellers affect supply
Student can explain how technology, input costs and weather affect supply
visualIdeas: a farmer’s supply shifting after a good monsoon

topics.title: Market Equilibrium
objectives: Student can find the equilibrium price where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied
Student can explain how excess demand and excess supply push prices toward equilibrium and how markets keep adjusting
visualIdeas: demand and supply curves crossing at the equilibrium point with shortage and surplus regions

topics.title: Role of Government in the Economy
objectives: Student can explain why governments regulate unfair practices, set price ceilings and floors, and provide public goods
Student can describe the limitations of government intervention
visualIdeas: a price ceiling line below equilibrium creating a shortage
